newsitem.title: USA: House defeats plan for campaign fundraising probe.
newsitem.headline: House defeats plan for campaign fundraising probe.

text.p: In a stunning rebuke to House Republican leaders, lawmakers Thursday narrowly defeated a plan to allocate millions of dollars to investigate White House fundraising abuses.
The House by a vote of 213-210 defeated a procedural motion before lawmakers could begin debate on the controversial funding measure.

Despite a day of frantic lobbying, House leaders were unable to quell revolt within their own party and lost needed Republican votes. Conservative Republicans said the overall funding legislation, which would provide money for all House committees, as well as the White House investigation, was simply too expensive.
"I'm not going to leave here this weekend with a sick feeling in my gut that I voted to increase spending," said Rep. Mark Neumann, a Wisconsin Republican.

Democrats charged the bill would have provided up to $20 million to the Government Reform panel for what they termed a partisan witchhunt into White House fundraising problems -- while ignoring congressional fundraising abuses.

The bill set aside $3.8 million for the Government Reform investigation. Democrats said the real price tag would be many times higher, partly because Republicans had created an $8 million fund the committee could dip into if needed.
After the loss on the rule, Republican leaders were meeting off the House floor to try to decide how to proceed.
